tasks.short: Visit schools to tutor and consult on special needs

steps.what: Read the school, sensory impairments and special needs in the pupil record ({OTHER}).
Draft an unsaved consultation record from that school, those impairments and those needs.
Check the impairments and special needs against the pupil record, then accept it.
File only the accepted consultation record in the pupil record ({OTHER}).
Visit the schools where these students are enrolled.
Tutor the students with sensory impairments during the visit.
Consult with the teachers regarding the students' special needs, in the room.

tasks.design: She reads the school, the sensory impairments and the special needs in the pupil record ({OTHER}). A deterministic step drafts an unsaved consultation record from those fields and stops. She checks that the impairments and the needs still match the pupil. A separate step files only the accepted record back into the pupil record. She still visits the schools, still tutors the students, and still consults the teachers in the room. Nothing is sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sensory impairments and the special needs sat in the pupil record, and she retyped them into the consultation entry before each visit.
tasks.enabler_now: The pupil record already stores the school, the sensory impairments and the special needs as fields a configured copy can lift.
tasks.still_hard: Tutoring a student with a sensory impairment, and what to tell the classroom teacher, are judgements in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She sees how the student works and what the classroom teacher can actually do that day.
tasks.altitude: The visits, the tutoring and the teacher talks stay hers. She no longer retypes the consultation entry, but she accepts it before it is filed, and she does not hand over the tutoring or the consultation.

reach.task: open the pupil record before the teacher visits a school
reach.learn: which sensory impairments and special needs the consultation record may copy, and that it must not add a diagnosis or change the support plan

evidence.claim: The school visit, the tutoring and the teacher consultation stay with her. The only shorter work is copying the recorded sensory impairments and special needs into a consultation record and filing the version she accepted. Model knowledge.
ParnasSys holds pupil records and an OPP module, and that page names no AI.
Support needs in a support plan are health data. The consultation record copies only the sensory impairments and special needs already stored, and it adds no new diagnosis. Model knowledge.
AI that admits pupils, evaluates learning outcomes, sets the education level or watches tests is high-risk.
The OPP is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and is evaluated yearly.
Under the WMS, staff consent to tools that can monitor them, and parents and pupils consent to pupil-data rules.

assumptions: The pupil record ({OTHER}) stores the school, the sensory impairments and the special needs. She reads them in s1. The draft in s2 copies only those fields and does not save. If a field is missing she types it in s3. The record adds no diagnosis and does not set or change the OPP.

The draft step only produces the unsaved consultation record and stops. It does not wait for a check of that output. She accepts the impairments and the needs in s3. s4 files only that accepted version. A wording change voids the filing.

The visit, the tutoring and the consultation are not shortened. Talking with a classroom teacher is inside the organisation. A report sent to another school would be its own gated step and is not built.
The 6 already-counted hours are the check in s3 and are not subtracted again. The 2 incremental hours are rewrites when she rejects a record.
No step infers a pupil's emotion. The record does not admit a pupil, grade work, set a level, or watch a test. It does not monitor staff.
unknowns: Whether this school's pupil record stores sensory impairments and special needs as fields, or only in prose.
Whether filing the consultation entry back into the pupil record needs a fresh parent consent.
research_questions: What share of consultation records she rejects because the sensory impairments changed after she read the pupil record.

already_counted.description: Checking the impairments and the special needs against the pupil record is already in s3.

incremental.description: Rewriting a rejected consultation record herself, beyond the check already in s3.

approvals.approved_version: Consultation record she accepted in s3: the school, the sensory impairments and the special needs copied from the pupil record she read, with no new diagnosis and no change to the support plan. A wording change voids it. The filing uses this version and no other.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a first-visit week the impairments are not fields, so she rewrites the consultation record and about 1 point remains after the 2 hours of rewrites. On a return-visit week the pupil record is stable and she accepts the draft, so drafting and filing are shorter, about 4. The 2 hours of rewrites are already off the central 7. The visit, the tutoring and the consultation stay hers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week is still the school visits, the tutoring and the talks with classroom teachers. She accepts the consultation record before it is filed in the pupil record. She does not hand over the tutoring or the consultation.
reach: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
skills_to_grow: Check a consultation record against the pupil record and reject any new diagnosis or any change to the support plan.
role.ambitious_version: The only change is the consultation record in the pupil record. It is filed only after she accepts that version. The school visits, the tutoring and the talks with classroom teachers stay hers.
